problem_type: Persisted terminal provider-adapter run has no user-controlled lifecycle
symptom: An API verification error remains visible after the connection is fixed or deleted and after restarting Nomi.
direct_cause: The provider adapter store persists terminal certification runs indefinitely, and the renderer bridge exposes list/get/cancel but no deletion path.
class_root: The shared persistence boundary does not distinguish active work from terminal history or provide a safe terminal-record cleanup operation.
affected_population: Users who encounter a failed, partial, cancelled, timed-out, stale, or needs-AI provider verification run
Users who later edit/delete the connection or restart the desktop app
entry_points: Manual provider connection verification task list
Persisted provider-adapter run reload after application restart
internal_only_reason: This invariant belongs to Nomi's internal persisted run lifecycle; no external provider contract decides whether a local historical verification record may be cleared.
invariants: Only terminal provider-adapter runs may be cleared.
Clearing a run removes it from persistent runs and leaves revisions, credentials, and catalog models untouched.
Active runs remain cancellable and cannot be deleted through the renderer bridge.
A stale or unknown run id fails closed with a stable RUN_NOT_FOUND response.
generality_proof: All provider-adapter verification callers persist and reload through ProviderAdapterStore and the canonical integration-certification IPC bridge. Enforcing terminal-only deletion at the store and service boundaries covers list rows, detail views, restart reloads, and future renderer callers without relying on vendor existence or UI filtering.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Atomically remove only a terminal run from provider-adapters.json.
Apply the run lifecycle check before delegating deletion and preserve active work.
Expose a stable, sender-guarded renderer boundary for terminal record cleanup.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: AdapterTaskList terminal row and AdapterTaskWorkspace terminal detail
same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both surfaces display persisted certification runs and will call the same delete bridge operation.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: Catalog lifecycle and promotion revision state
same_class_entry_points.evidence: The fix intentionally preserves active revisions and catalog entries; only historical run records change.

recurrence.reason: Every failed or partial verification can create a terminal record, and every restart or task-list reload rehydrates that record unless the shared lifecycle boundary removes it.
same_class_scan: Inspected ProviderAdapterStore persistence and reload paths
Inspected catalog vendor/model deletion paths and confirmed they do not own certification history
Inspected task list and terminal detail entry points

prevention.invariant: Persistent run deletion is permitted only for terminal stages and is atomic.
prevention.failure_mode: Active runs return RUN_ACTIVE and unknown ids return RUN_NOT_FOUND; no partial state is written.
prevention.strategy: Make the persistent store the earliest shared owner of terminal history lifecycle, then expose the same invariant through service and IPC layers.

legacy_paths.rationale: There is no obsolete code path to remove; the fix adds an explicit terminal-record lifecycle while preserving active work and revisions.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the local provider-adapter run lifecycle invariant.

migration: No migration is needed. Existing terminal records remain until the user clears them, and active/revision state is unchanged.
residual_risks: This fix does not introduce automatic retention expiry; users must clear old terminal records explicitly.
Real Electron click-through validation must confirm the renderer bridge is wired in the packaged desktop entry point.
